location: Rosebud, Nevada — "The Original Water-Wagon" Novelty Postcard
notes: Undivided-back era postcard — the U.S. didn't allow divided backs (message + address on same side) until March 1907, so the message is squeezed directly onto the illustrated front. Front is a comic 'temperance' illustration titled THE ORIGINAL WATER-WAGON, showing Noah's Ark reimagined as a wagon being towed by a sea serpent, a nod to the popular early-1900s phrase 'on the water wagon' (teetotaling). 1¢ Franklin green stamp. Postmarked with a partial Missouri origin cancel dated Jul 25 1907, with a second postmark reading ROSEBUD JUL 29 P.M. NEV. — likely the receiving/backstamp at the Nevada end. Rosebud was a short-lived early-1900s Nevada mining camp. Message: 'Hello Papa: I know you like to get postals. Make a collection for me. Be good to your self. Received your postals, hope you are getting along all right, let us hear from you soon, am well. will write a letter nothing to write on a postal. good bye Viola.'

year: c. 1963–1968 (dated by stamp, not postmark — see notes)
recipient: Misses Carol and Irene Morris, 16400 Canfield St. N.E., Alliance, Ohio, Rt. #5
notes: Night View of Fontana Dam — F B11, photographed by Gene Aikens, published by W.M. Cline Co., Chattanooga, TN, copyright 1956, card #18261. The 1956 copyright line is the card's print year, not necessarily its mailing year — postcard racks commonly sold stock for years after printing. Postmark reads '...NKLIN...N.C.' (Franklin, NC) but the date within the cancel is illegible under foxing/staining even under magnification. The stamp is more reliable: a 5¢ Washington (Liberty Series, Scott #1213), issued Nov. 1962 and used for the 5¢ first-class rate 1963–1968 — which places the actual mailing in that window, several years after the card's 1956 print date. Message: 'Pretty huh!!! Hi! We were at Fontana Dam this afternoon. Took several pic. Boy the roads are straight, they go like this [drawing of a squiggle] — over 200 curves in 20 miles. We'll be down at Bear Pen on ___ and send you post cards from there. Until then Bye. Mary Ellen & Nancy. Tell everybody Hi!' POSSIBLE FAMILY NETWORK NODE: recipient 'Irene Morris' reappears as an adult ('Irene D. Morris') on the 1981 Joshua Tree card (#173), then living in Canton, Ohio — about 20 miles from this Alliance, OH address. Worth tagging as the same person if you want to build out the Griswold Trips connection.

address: Sheridan Rd & Foster Ave, Chicago, IL 60640
recipient: Mrs. Anna Robinson, Oak Grove, Mo.
notes: The Sands Motel, Chicago — AAA-rated, 150 air-conditioned rooms with 21-inch television, adjoining the Edgewater Beach Hotel, Sheridan Rd & Foster Ave. Front shows an aerial view of the motel's pool/parking court with the Edgewater Beach Hotel towers behind it and a 'Peter Pan' snack shop sign in the foreground. Three 1¢ Washington (Liberty series) stamps; Chicago postmark JUL 20 1959, plus a transit backstamp from Berrien Springs, Mich. Message describes a whirlwind day of Chicago sightseeing: church, Chinatown, Maxwell Street Market, Hull House, the Palmer House, the Drake Hotel, the Museum of Science and Industry, the Art Institute, then swimming in Lake Michigan — with a plan to spend the next day at Arlington Park race track.
recipientLocationNote: There's more than one 'Oak Grove' in Missouri — pinned the better-known one near Kansas City (Jackson/Lafayette Co.); flag if you know it's the other.

recipient: Frau Hildegard Hueskel, 509 Ave. of Oaks, Houston 22, Texas
notes: "Gruss aus Königswinter" multi-view card: the Drachenfels castle ruin, Drachenfels und Drachenburg, Rheininsel Nonnenwerth, the Autofähre (car ferry) between Mehlem and Königswinter, and Petersberg, framed around the town's coat of arms. Back is a German-language letter dated 7.7.60 (European day-month-year format = July 7, 1960) — opens 'Meine liebe Hilde!' ('My dear Hilde!') and appears to be a birthday letter ('zu Deinem Geburtstag' / 'for your birthday'). No stamp or postmark visible in this scan. Address uses the pre-ZIP postal zone number 'Houston 22, Texas' (zone numbers were phased out when ZIP codes launched in 1963). Full transcription is tentative — this is handwritten German cursive and would benefit from a native-German read for accuracy.
